description: Minimax picks a move in a two-player game by assuming that the opponent always answers with its best move. It searches every line to a fixed depth and scores the positions there with an evaluation function, from the point of view of the side *Max*. Going back up, *Max* takes the highest child score and *Min* the lowest. The side to move belongs to the position, so one side may move several times in a row. Minimax visits every position of the tree, so it serves as a reference; use alpha-beta pruning for the same score at far lower cost.

papers.title: Programming a computer for playing chess
papers.venue: The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science
